author: .just_kk
content:
<@&595681771690000403> hello! Responding to the commend in ACDC zoom chat.

We discussed this EIP a lot on the p2p breakouts and similar ideas were discussed for years.  We can justify any design decisions if you think this EIP is still not mature enough.

Glamsterdam increases the gas limit and Hegota potentially decreases slot time. Also we need to make room for additional traffic that PQ will bring + similar machinery will be used for proofs propagation.

The scope is minimal and does not require any networking stack changes. Most of the EIP is just chunking the message + introducing one field in the bid.

Happy to reiterate on any detail if you had any particular concerns. Or if you need some additional data to be convinced of necessity of the EIP let us know

author: matthewkeil
content:
ill be honest, im not a big fan of the feature. it feels like a premature optimization.

i also dont really agree that its a minimal change. there is no "partial" gossip anything that is "minimal".  the switch from blobs to columns was a massive lift.  and from columns to cell-DAS was as well

i think when we see mainnet data on how payloads actually propagate i will be easier to convince though

author: .just_kk
content:
Some gossip data
https://investigations.ethpandaops.io/2026-05/block-size-vs-propagation/

So around ~800-900ms for ~200KB blocks. In the past there were blocks of size ~1MB.
Glamsterdam increases the limits and adds the BALs so payloads will get larger. We could easily expect 300-500KB blocks. 
With EIP-7870 nodes (which is the worst case assumption) in our simulations it takes ~4 seconds to reach 95% of nodes.

The main change is splitting the serialized envelope into 64 chunks and just sending them into the topic. It is nowhere near to the PeerDAS complexity

author: .just_kk
content: We're so much inefficient today by downloading the full payload before we forward it further. We're getting 3-4x latency decrease if we send individual chunks and can start forwarding them before we received the full message

author: vladimir_ea
content:
From a builder perspective faster block propagation is critical (especially given the somewhat squeezed timeframe for execution payload dispersal in Gloas..).

Without a change like this and with increased gas and BALs as noted, there is going to be increased risk of empty slots.

author: vladimir_ea
content: what advantage is there in delayed publishing of execution payload? there are no timing games - the payload is locked in by beacon block - tje only reason to delay is to observe enough attestations to be sure that the block is going to land

author: nflaig
content: yes I know it works, I am not talking about that

author: vladimir_ea
content:
> builders will likely delay publishing anyways to the last second to get an advantage over other builders, so this time would get eaten up by payload timing games most likely
so what are you talking about here? what are the timing games that relate to payload propagation?

author: vladimir_ea
content: you appear ot be making an argument against implementing a change to payload propagation based on the fact that builders will play timing games? not sure i understand what the argument is?

author: vladimir_ea
content: from a builder pov having faster payload propagation is "a good thing" because it increases certainty that blocks will land: more time ot observe attestations = more chance of reaching certainty = fewer missed slots

author: sky.cactus
content: Builders profit more by building a block later, as more transactions will be available to fill their block with.  If propagation is slow, then builders submit earlier in their window.  If propagation is fast, they submit later in their window.

author: sky.cactus
content: Fast propagation only really helps reduce missed slots if the time to propagate is close to the time builders have to build a block.  Anything shorter should result in the same number of missed slots because builders are optimizing for a sufficiently low rate of missed slots so they are net profitable with late submission profit vs missed slot losses.

author: vladimir_ea
content: So that might be the case currently for Fulu but is absolutely not the case for payload propagation under Gloas, which is the context for this EIP.

author: vladimir_ea
content: And just for the sake of clarity, it is not currently builders that play timing games it is the proposers delaying fetching the block from the relay in order to maximise their payment - that can still occur under Gloas, proposers may delay fetching bids from direct builder connections. But that only indirectly impacts execution payload propagation.

author: vladimir_ea
content: Under current PBS it is the proposer who closes the ‘auction’ by calling ‘getPayload’ on a relay, builders send blocks to relays they have no say on the timing

author: vladimir_ea
content: There is zero incentive to delay propagating execution payload under Gloas, in fact it’s the opposite: once a builder’s bid is accepted and the beacon block is gossiped it’s in their interest to send the payload as soon as it is safe to do so. And the faster it goes the better- better for the builder and I think better for everyone

author: nflaig
content: well if a payload takes close to 6 seconds to execute then other builders can prepare a payload on top of that at the start of the slot so they have ~1 second to built their payload and submit a bid, while the builder that built the payload of previous slot has much more time, if you are saying this is not an advantage for the previous slot builder I am gonna believe you, I don't wanna derail the discussion here, like I said above, I don't have a strong opinion on this EIP

author: vladimir_ea
content: payload takes 6 seconds to execute? I have a beacon node using Ethrex as the EL and it takes *at most* 180ms to validate the block (normally around 30ms). And validating the block is executing it: you have to execute transactions in order on top of the current state, collect the state changes, apply them and calculate the state root.

author: vladimir_ea
content: execution payload must *arrive* at 6s into the slot (voted by PTC), so everyone sees the execution payload 6 seconds before the end of the slot.

author: vladimir_ea
content: anyway, I don't know an argument that slow propagation is somehow fairer actually bears much scrutiny - slower propagation means the interval between first receivers and last receivers of the payload is greater - which seems *less* fair in terms of time available to act on it.

author: vladimir_ea
content: most fair would be instantaneous arrival everywhere
